newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban Red Cross distributes Canadian aid.
newsitem.headline: Cuban Red Cross distributes Canadian aid.

text.p: Cuban Red Cross officials on Thursday began distributing blankets and other aid donated by the Canadian Red Cross to Cuban families whose homes were damaged by Hurricane Lili.
Needy familes in Jaguey Grande in Matanzas province, about 90 miles (150 km) southeast of Havana, were given sets of blankets, as well as tablets to purify water and rehydration salts.

The aid arrived in Havana on Wednesday on a Canadian air force C-130 transport plane. Some of the cargo, worth a total of $50,000, was also to be sent to families in Cienfuegos and Villa Clara provinces.
Douglas Remer, a Canadian Red Cross official who accompanied the cargo, told reporters in Jaguey Grande the Red Cross was pleased to have been able to get relief rapidly to affected families.

Hurricane Lili swept through central and western areas of communist-ruled Cuba on Oct. 17-18. Authorities have said the storm destroyed some 5,000 homes and damaged crops, power lines and communications.

Mexico has sent two planeloads of medicines, food and roofing materials, as well as a boat with a plant to purify water. Spain has promised some $200,000 in aid and the European Union has pledged relief worth some $800,000.

The Cuban American community in the United States also mobilised to send food. But a planeload of rice, beans and milk sent by U.S. donors last Saturday was still in a warehouse in Havana, delayed by bureaucratic problems.

Father Thomas Wenski, an official of Miami Roman Catholic archdiocese that channelled the aid to a Cuban church charity, said on Thursday the cargo of some 30 tonnes had not yet been transported to central city of Cienfuegos, where it is meant to be distributed. He said discussions with authorities were continuing.
